Real estate tip

Three deal notes: how the numbers changed the decision

Worked examples of the checks I run before an offer and before a list price. The situations are typical; the figures are examples.

Ali Bayat
Figures checked against the sources below on November 21, 2026
Published November 26, 2026
Illustrative examplesNot client filesUpdated November 2026

These are illustrative examples, not past client files. The situations are typical and the prices, fees and sales figures are example numbers used to show the method. They are not real transactions or results.

01Note 1: The condo that said wait

Two similar condos near Finch. The cheaper one had a status certificate with warning signs: a reserve fund well short of the repair study, fees about to rise, and a special assessment already approved. Over five years the cheaper unit costs more.

Five-year cost (example)Unit AUnit B
Purchase price$688,000$705,000
Monthly fee$880$690
Fees over 60 months$52,800$41,400
Approved special assessment$12,000$0
Total$752,800$746,400

Example figures. Unit A looks $17,000 cheaper on price and ends up $6,400 more expensive, before any further fee increases. The status certificate is where this shows up. How to read one.

02Note 2: Pricing off last spring's sales

A North York bungalow priced from sales that were five months old. The market had moved, and every month on the market stale carries a real cost.

Price source (example)Indicated value
Sales from five months ago$1,580,000
Sales from the last 60 days, adjusted for lot and condition$1,490,000
Difference$90,000, or 5.7%
Carrying cost per month while listed (mortgage interest, tax, utilities)$9,400

Example figures. Overpricing by 5.7% and sitting for three months costs about $28,200 in carrying costs alone, before any price reduction. That's why I price from the most recent comparables.

03Note 3: The cheaper house that cost more

A buyer compares a $1,000,000 home south of Steeles with a $985,000 home north of it. The $15,000 gap in price is the small number.

At closing (example)South of Steeles (Toronto)North of Steeles (York Region)
Price$1,000,000$985,000
Ontario land transfer tax$16,475$16,175
Toronto municipal land transfer tax$16,475$0
Price plus land transfer tax$1,032,950$1,001,175

Land transfer tax computed from the 2026 schedules on the guide, with no rebates. The all-in gap is $31,775, more than twice the price difference. Property tax and carrying costs still need comparing; the calculator has fields for both.

Ali's take

A decision looks different once closing costs, carrying costs and risk are on the same page as the price. That's the work.
